heading: INT. CITY PAROLE OFFICE - RECEPTION - MORNING

units.text: INT. CITY PAROLE OFFICE - RECEPTION - MORNING
A beige room full of bad lighting and worse chairs.
Two teenagers in the corner share earbuds and a bag of chips.
A janitor's mop bucket sits unattended by the water cooler.
Frankie Dunn, 30s, charming and doomed, bursts through the door with a coffee in each hand and a paper bag in his teeth.
He trips over the mop bucket.
Water SLOSHES across the floor.
Mmf! Mmmf!
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: He spits the bag out.
Behind the desk, Officer Priya Nair, 30s, unflappable and unimpressed, looks up from a stack of files.
Mr. Dunn. You're eleven minutes late.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Priya! Officer Priya! Light of my life! I brought you a latte, the good kind, with the little heart in the foam.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: It's a cortado. And I'm not a morning person.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: I know. That's why I got two. One for you, one for me, one for the guy who's gonna ask me why I brought two.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: That's three, Frankie.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Is it? Huh. I only have two hands.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: He slips on the wet floor, the coffees fly, and both cups SPLAT against the wall.
The teenagers gasp.
One of them films it.
Whoa.
units.name: THE TEENAGERS

units.text: Frankie. Sit down.
units.name: PRIYA
paren: pinching the bridge of her nose

units.text: Yes, ma'am. Absolutely, ma'am. Sitting.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: He plops into a chair.
It COLLAPSES with a CRACK.
He lands on the floor, legs in the air.
I'm adding that to the report.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Priya. I need to tell you something.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: You need to give me your check-in form.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: I have it. It's in my pocket. It's a little wet.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: He fishes out a soggy paper ball and holds it up like a trophy.
She takes it between two fingers.
This is a tax receipt for a hot dog.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: It was a very good hot dog.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: You are the worst parolee I have ever had.
units.name: PRIYA
paren: finally, a crack of a smile

units.text: But am I your favorite?
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: That's not a thing.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: That is totally a thing. You're smiling.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: I'm not.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: You are! Your whole face is doing it.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: The door BANGS open.
THE GUARDS, two enormous men in matching uniforms, stand in the frame.
Everything okay in here?
units.name: THE GUARDS

units.text: Fine. Mr. Dunn was just leaving.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: I was? Oh. I was. Yes. Leaving. Great. Love that for me.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: Thursday. Ten sharp. Bring a real receipt.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Bring you a coffee too?
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: Just the one this time, Frankie.
units.name: PRIYA
paren: sighing, a warmth she can't hide

units.text: One coffee, Priya. One. You got it.
units.name: FRANKIE

units.text: He steps in the mop bucket again.
The BUCKET CLANGS.
The door SLAMS behind him.
The teenagers burst into applause.
Unbelievable.
units.name: PRIYA
paren: to the room, under her breath

units.text: She picks up the soggy receipt, studies it, and tucks it into her drawer instead of the trash.
